title: A tiny test runner
description:
Write an annotation and a runner:

- `@Retention(RUNTIME) @Target(METHOD) public @interface Check { String value(); }` in `Check.java`.
- `class Runner` with `static List<String> run(Object target)` that finds the target's declared methods annotated with `@Check`, sorts them by method name, calls each (they take no arguments) and returns one line per check:
  - `"pass <description>"` when the method returns normally (whatever it returns);
  - `"FAIL <description>: <message>"` when it throws, where the message is the **real** exception's `getMessage()` (unwrap the `InvocationTargetException`);
  - private methods are run too (`setAccessible(true)`).
- A method annotated with `@Check` that takes parameters gives `"SKIP <description>: needs arguments"`.
hints: Without `@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)`, `getAnnotation(Check.class)` always returns `null`, and the runner finds nothing.
`Method.invoke` wraps the method's exception: catch `InvocationTargetException` and report `e.getCause().getMessage()`.
